newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan opposition faction denounces allies' move.
newsitem.headline: Afghan opposition faction denounces allies' move.

text.p: The Hezb-i-Islami opposition faction of former Afghan prime minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar on Friday denounced a new cabinet announced by its allies parallel to the Taleban movement government in Kabul.

A Hezb statement, quoted by a Pakistan-based Afghan news service, called Wednesday's announcement of the new cabinet without any Hezb representation and based in the northern town of Mazar-i-Sharif as designed to divide Afghanistan.
Hekmatyar was the prime minister in the previous cabinet of opposition president Burhanuddin Rabbani, who was ousted by Taleban from Kabul in September last year.
In the new lineup, Rabbani remains president but the prime minister's job is given to former foreign minister Abdul Rahim Ghafourzai.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted the Hezb as saying this move would not benefit Afghanistan or the northern alliance, which also included Rabbani's Jamiat-i-Islami faction, Jumbush-i-Milli of Uzbek leader General Abdul Malik and Hezb-i-Wahdat of Shi'ite Moslems.
"We believe that Kabul is the capital of Afghanistan and we will support only that government which is based on the will of the people and controls the whole country," it said.

It said the Afghan problem could be solved only through talks, and called for a ceasefire between the warring sides, exchange of prisoners and establishment of neutral government and a national army to supervise elections.

Hezb-i-Islami was one of the major guerrilla groups that fought the Soviet occupation of Afghanistan in the 1980s, but it has lost control of territory in the past year, mostly to the fundamentalist Taleban militia which now controls more than two thirds of the country.
